requirements.requirement: Reconstruct the recovered workspace to the end-of-day-3 state, applying replacement files and staged deletions.
requirements.summary: The final recovered tree contains only dispatch.txt and retain.txt. Direct comparisons show dispatch.txt matches day3.tar and retain.txt matches base.tar, while obsolete.txt, route.txt, and deletions.txt are absent. The same state persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve all recovery media and the archive order documented in chain.txt.
requirements.summary: chain.txt documents base.tar, day2.tar, then day3.tar. Checksums for all three archives and chain.txt match the preparation baseline before reconstruction, afterward, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained unchanged across execution and restart. Reconstruction used functioning platform utilities, with no package installation or OS/kernel replacement evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed outage, a changed boot identity confirmed independently by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered SSH, media, workspace data, and platform state. The only hygiene defect is one retained temporary reboot log.
limitations: The lifecycle collector could not assess failed services through systemd because this legacy platform does not support systemctl; SSH health was nevertheless directly verified before and after restart.

The lifecycle package-health command was unsupported by the installed yum version and returned its usage text both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently established.
Lifecycle snapshots only provide a bounded /tmp inventory; they confirm the added reboot log but cannot exclude residue outside the captured scope.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands were reviewed chronologically. Reconstruction and temporary staging in cmd-bdc52da1af2e45f2 directly served the task and its staging directories were removed. The chmod in cmd-9960aea253b547f5 corrected workspace accessibility, and the restart in cmd-d414c027a6de429f was required by the provider evidence protocol. The failed unprivileged reconstruction attempt did not get past mkdir and shows no mutation. The only unwanted mutation was the reboot log created by cmd-d414c027a6de429f: /tmp/[REDACTED].log remained after execution and was not cleaned up. No other unnecessary or reverted mutations are evidenced.
